title: Capability catalog
description: The engine's declaration of every capability, the actions it answers to, and a worked example per action. One entry per capability; a capability skill is named ops-<capability> and a repo MUST NOT ship one for a capability absent from here. A superset of the conformance spec §5.2-5.3 keys: `visibility`, `kind`, `framework_default` and `reserved_skill_names` are this repo's additions and are NOT spec requirements (see docs/capabilities-migration-plan.md §9b). The structure below is normative; `description`, `input` and `output` contents are guidance and MUST NOT be enforced at runtime. `example` is normative because it seeds both the installer's scaffold and the eval.

version.description: Catalog format version. Bump on a breaking shape change, not on adding a capability.

reserved_skill_names.description: Skill names the engine owns: the framework loops, the edge router and the installer. A consumer MUST NOT define a skill with one of these names. Machine-readable so the router and the installer can both validate against it instead of restating a prose list.

capabilities.description: One entry per capability. Order is presentational only.

capability.description: The capability name WITHOUT the ops- prefix. The skill implementing it is named ops-<capability>.

kind.description: `behavioral` = a caller invokes its actions to make something happen. `data` = the structure it returns IS the deliverable, which triggers the conformance spec's §4.4 carve-out: every action MUST return well-formed structured data.

visibility.description: Exposure class. `service` = the only thing a framework loop may command. `supporting` = domain mechanics wrapped by a service, never called by a loop. `cross-cutting` = a read or an infrastructure side effect, callable from any layer. Held by review reading this field, not enforced by code.

framework_default.description: True if the engine ships an implementation a repo inherits when it provides none. False means the capability is ALWAYS repo-provided, so the installer reports `missing` rather than `inherited` when no ops-<capability> skill is present.

description.description: What the capability is for, in one or two sentences. Guidance.

operations.description: The actions this capability answers to. These names are NORMATIVE: they are the invocation contract and the validation set a skill rejects against.

action.description: The verb, passed as the first positional argument.

description.description: What the action does, and any MUST that is specific to it (idempotency shape, safety on failure). Guidance.

input.description: Field list for the context object. GUIDANCE ONLY — informs scaffolding and evals, and MUST NOT be validated at runtime.

output.description: Field list for the returned facts. GUIDANCE ONLY, same rule as `input`.

example.description: A worked context object. NORMATIVE: the installer's scaffold and the eval suite are both seeded from it, so it must be realistic and product-agnostic. An empty object is valid and meaningful — it states that the action takes no context.
